name: Deals
title: Deals: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Start a restaurant offer and decide what the guest must do to qualify.
Choose the buy items, discounted items and calculation.
Choose dates, service hours, order sources and code restrictions.
Save a draft or activate the completed deal.
Follow the offer through online and device checkout.
End or archive an offer and check discounted sales.

NODES.d: Open Deals for the intended restaurant and inspect existing offers before creating another.
e: An archived offer with the same promotion is overlooked

NODES.d: Choose discount, buy this get this, gift with purchase, or gift without purchase in the classic flow.
e: Changing type retains items from the previous type
A gift without purchase is configured when a purchase is required

NODES.d: Set dollars or percentage off and choose the entire order or selected products. Check the effective price on a low value basket.
e: A percentage is interpreted as dollars
Guest is charged the wrong amount
A fixed discount exceeds the eligible line value

NODES.d: For a buy and get offer, choose which purchases and quantities count. A gift with purchase also needs its qualifying conditions.
e: Quantity from an excluded item contributes to the threshold
Two qualifying units on separate lines fail to combine

NODES.d: Choose which products receive the saving or gift. A gift without purchase can be configured without a buy group.
e: Buy items are saved as reward items
The only reward is later removed from the menu
Offer is advertised but cannot be completed

NODES.d: The service stores menu, category or individual item selections for buy and get groups. Check partial category selections separately.
e: Limit on individually selected items prevents choosing only part of a large category
Operator must narrow or broaden the offer
Selecting a full category accidentally includes a newly added premium item

NODES.d: When enabled, configure the minimum spend or item quantity and test the basket immediately below, at and above the threshold.
e: A basket one cent below minimum qualifies
Price changes leave a previously eligible basket below the threshold without an explanation

NODES.d: Check the paid add-ons on a reward item. The Android POS receipt calculates the item deal on the reward line using its base price and quantity. Compare the add-on charges and final amount with the ticket. Verify the online calculation separately.
e: Discount on a free base item also removes paid extras unexpectedly
Checkout and receipt assign different prices to the same modified reward

NODES.d: Buy this get this separates Minimum Item Count from the number of items that receive a discount. Check both with mixed eligible items and repeated quantities.
e: Two qualifying purchases produce two discounted units where the offer promises one
The last eligible unit is ignored when the qualifying quantity sits on separate order lines

NODES.d: Select the start and end dates. The classic form can constrain the selectable weekdays for a single day or date range.
e: A one day deal is inactive for its intended day
Restaurant midnight is calculated using the operator's time zone
Offer starts or ends on the wrong date

NODES.d: Set the applicable weekdays and the hour window. Check eligibility at opening, closing and across a service day boundary.
e: An order exactly at the end time receives the expired price
Offer stays visible outside its chosen weekdays
Guests cannot complete an advertised offer

NODES.d: The classic choices include POS with mPOS, Kiosk, QR and Website. Availability is calculated for the requesting order source.
e: A kiosk-only offer also appears online
mPOS does not receive an offer selected under the shared POS label

NODES.d: Set a recognisable name, description, guest terms and optional images. The classic image field allows up to five images.
e: Duplicate name blocks saving after the operator completes the form
Guest description promises a different quantity from the configured reward

NODES.d: When a code is enabled, check its availability and configure its permitted use. Verify typed and generated codes against the intended restaurant.
e: An existing code resolves to a different offer
A limited-use code is accepted on two simultaneous checkouts after the last use

NODES.d: Review the terms, eligibility and placement. Save an unfinished offer as Draft or submit at the final step.
e: Preview price excludes a qualification shown only in configuration
Incomplete settings survive submission as an active deal

NODES.d: Locate the saved draft, restore the selected products and recheck availability before submission.
e: A selected menu item is deleted between draft and release
Draft reopens with wider scope than the saved subset
Discount is applied to too many items

NODES.d: The service chooses Active or Scheduled based on the dates and schedules status transitions. Drafts do not schedule activation.
e: Scheduled start is missed while the deal remains Scheduled
An earlier end event survives a schedule edit

NODES.d: Deal availability depends on the offer dates, channel and linked campaign status. Android POS refreshes active, unarchived offers using the device date and time. A failed refresh puts the list into a failed state. For campaign-linked deals, all linked campaigns must meet the Active or Sent rule.
e: The register clock falls outside the offer window during a refresh
Staff may miss a valid deal or see it at the wrong time
An active deal is missing from one ordering channel
One linked campaign is still in review when the restaurant expects its deal to appear
An otherwise active offer is missing

NODES.t: Open an online or QR offer
NODES.d: Open the deal from a restaurant listing or link. The online details page can show an unavailable state when the offer cannot be claimed. Campaign audience groups are combined across groups, with alternatives allowed inside a group. The online ordering check omits spend.
e: Deep link opens a different restaurant or unavailable deal
Listing advertises an offer whose only eligible item is unavailable

NODES.d: Select the qualifying items and rewards, or enter the promo code where required. Compare eligible value with the displayed minimum spend.
e: Removing a qualifying item leaves the free item discounted
Guest pays less than the configured price
Qualifying spend includes an ineligible line or fee

NODES.d: On Android POS the cashier selects an offer in Deals and Discounts. The register checks offer terms and qualifying spend, then applies a ticket discount or opens item selection as appropriate. Check mPOS and Kiosk separately.
e: POS applies a deal the guest cannot see on the receipt
The register blocks the selected offer without making clear which existing discount conflicts with it
The cashier cannot tell which discount to remove

NODES.d: On Android POS, compare the discount against the paid receipt. Item deals appear on the reward line and entire-ticket deals appear in the totals. For online orders, compare the buy, get and loyalty lines against the displayed total, tax and fees.
e: Rebuilding an order summary subtracts an entire-order discount twice
Amount displayed differs from amount charged
Rounding across two discounted quantities changes tax or final cents

NODES.d: On Android POS, check the offer terms when applying a deal to a ticket with an existing deal or discount. If the guest also uses a loyalty reward or pays by gift card, reconcile the reward line, the discount and the tender separately.
e: A loyalty line receives a second unintended reduction
Restaurant pays twice for one reward
Gift card tender is treated as another price discount
Balance due or tax is wrong

NODES.d: If the cashier voids a qualifying item, Android POS rechecks the required items and minimum spend and can remove the deal. Compare the revised ticket and paid receipt. For a channel that accepts promo codes, check the remaining uses after a failed payment.
e: Declined payment consumes the last permitted code use
Guest cannot retry a valid offer
Paid receipt shows the undiscounted total

NODES.d: Reopen the supported edit flow. Verify saved scope, dates and guest-facing copy after changing a deal.
e: New dates save while old availability remains on devices
Different prices for the same offer
Editing one offer changes the terms on a historic receipt
Audit trail no longer matches payment

NODES.d: End marks the deal complete and records the current end time. Check saved links, devices and attached marketing messages. Ending a campaign placement leaves its underlying deal subject to the deal status and dates.
e: Old campaign link still implies the promotion is redeemable
A cart opened before ending retains the expired saving at payment

NODES.d: Archive controls list visibility and eligibility. On restore, verify the underlying status and dates before promotion.
e: Restoring visibility is mistaken for reopening an expired deal
Historical results disappear from an operator's filtered view

NODES.d: Compare the amount actually charged for discounted items with the refund and receipt. For a limited-use promo code, check the remaining uses in the service after the refund.
e: Refund uses full menu price on a discounted item
Code is reinstated after a partial refund that retained the reward
Guest can claim the offer again

NODES.d: Compare Deals sold and Revenue in Marketing Overview to the paid tickets for the same period and location.
e: A buy item and free item both count as separate redemptions
Refunded value remains in an otherwise net revenue comparison

NODES.d: Confirm the final guest price, offer status or report against the original offer terms.
e: Verification uses the displayed discount but omits the paid receipt

NOTES: The classic deal flow and server availability rules are mapped. Extra controls introduced only by the flow flag are excluded.
PROD 4673 records the partial-category item-selection limitation. The current numeric limit was not established. PROD 4898 concerns POS meal break reminders, so it is not deal redemption evidence.

Android POS internal d2b5329 was checked in DealsRepositoryImpl, DealsAndDiscountViewModel, validator.kt and TicketReceiptMapper. Offer refresh, cashier selection and receipt rules are visible in the app. Code-use restoration and the mPOS and Kiosk implementations require separate evidence.
